calls.body: It’s the Stars’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Predators get more of the play than usual.

calls.body: On shot quality, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Nashville is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should be the Stars’.

surprises.head: Dallas couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Dallas usually gets some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Not tonight: a 4.2% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.9% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 90 games.

story.head: The Predators squeak past the Stars
paras: Miro Heiskanen got the scoring started for the Stars just 47 seconds into the game, but they didn’t score again. Steven Stamkos made it 1-1 for Nashville on the power play just under four minutes later. Nils Höglander scored his first goal for Nashville on the power play late in the first to put the Predators ahead for good. Jack Ahcan made his Predators debut, after two seasons with the Avalanche, and picked up an assist.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Juuse Saros made 29 saves for the Predators, and Casey DeSmith stopped 24 of 26. The Preds improved to 1-1-0, climbing out of last place in the NHL. The Stars fell to 0-2-0, still last in the NHL.
